As soon as breakfast was finished Stan took down the small "buggy" that had been folded up inside it's compartment accessed from underneath the ship. Despite it's lightweight tubular frame feeling a little flimsy the actual capacity of the small vehicle was incredible, easily able to fill all three of it's seats with full-grown adults. Unfortunately it didn't quite have the offroad capability as newer vehicles of the same type, but he knew it well enough to remember all it could do and where it's limits were.

Instead of using some sort of electrical drive or nuclear-powered propulsion, it relied entirely on hydrocarbon fuel that the Kriegsmark produced specifically for the occasion. Part gas, part liquid, the fuel system was known commercially as "meth-octo propulsion" and could deliver incredible performance at the cost of being smelly and harmful to whatever environment it was in. Obviously for use in rarefied atmosphere the O2 bottle had to be used, but normally Stan just used that to give it some extra boost and damn did it do that. Surging across the field was done with the slightest pressure on the pedal and the front tires lept from the dirt with happy enthusiasm; the surprise earned him an angry swat from his surly mate.

"Teekus slow down!"

"Hell no!" he yelled back, laughing as the front tires rattled over a patch of sandy gravel.

Some genius had built the thing with a handbrake too, as if there wasn't enough temptation to dick around in the thing the moment a guy got behind the wheel. Whenever he got the opportunity to use it he abused that nifty feature to hell and back, a yank caused the wheels to lock and the vehicle skidded to the side before being allowed to complete the turn with all the torque the little tri-rotor wankel cycle engine could deliver. They didn't come with much of a muffler, it sounded like a gigantic insect on tearing through the forest. In the mirror he could see that the muffler had turned a nice, cherry-red shade and had to smirk knowing how goddamn hot that was. Wasteful as all hell but the power coming out of such a tiny little engine.

Ahead he saw a fallen log and downshifted, letting the resistance in the engine do the work of slowing him down before he hit the brakes. They coasted for a few meters as he gauged the distance, and at the last possible moment he stomped the accelerator and lifted the front end up and over the obstacle. Immediately after that he goosing it hard so the back tires gripped the obstacle and climbed it, a maneuver that made the entire vehicle rocket upward and forward as the engine whined loudly through the air. This was a better position for them, had he let the vehicle jostle and bounce off the log it would have likely caused the back end to buck up with the front tires still on the ground; a terrible condition that would probably test the rollcage and break a few arms.

Mad laughter bubbled out of him as he found a wide footpath marked by ruts from travois poles, the perfect place to really open it up, and he shifted to a higher gear before flooring it. Again the front tires tried to lift off the ground, but they were already moving fast enough to make that an impossibility. Far off to the right he could see a stunned group of villagers with woven baskets staring in shocked silence as they roared past, a good sign they were near the village, and a few more minutes of driving revealed a collection of buildings made from field stones and logs topped with sod.

Of course the villagers didn't know what the hell to think, but they were smart enough to get the hell out of the way as the nimble vehicle blew past them and into the village center. Off to his right Inzili was livid but he couldn't hear her bitching, he was focused, a quick dart of his eyes to assess the situation was all he needed.

"Hold on!"

Cranking the steering wheel he yanked the handbrake and caused the vehicle to spin, letting it go just long enough to coast for a meter before mashing the pedal into the floor. They bounced along the coarse sand before finally coming to a stop, the roar of the engine ceased as he turned the key.

Annabelle would stay in her scabbard for the moment, with Inzili and Jhoka he felt confident enough to climb out of the vehicle and stand in plain sight.

"Teekus you fucking asshole," she snarled, standing on the other side with a furious glare. "They never seen this before, why you scare! Think!"

Stan shrugged and motioned to a particularly terrified group huddled near a small hut, the crowd bristling with spears. "They're not rushin' us, best to come on in big and loud."

"You not needed to doing this, you take me with to translate remember? Asshole!"

"Damn, it's not a big deal, come on," he paused to smile at the people. "See? They're fine."

Obviously they were not fine and she needed to clean up his mess. Turning to the pair of villagers nearest to her she mustered up the most saccharine tone she could manage. "Sorry for my mate, he does not think sometimes. We greet you."

"They came to help my father," Jhoka added, climbing down from her seat. "They brought medicine for him."

"Jhoka!"

A familiar giant pushed her way through the crowd to give the young huntress a one-armed hug. "I should have known it was you. Zuua, her mate... I forget his name. Why have you come?"

"My father is sick, Khojaewa. They bring medicine."

Inzili smiled up at the tower of muscle and held out a small bag. "I've brought these for your children."

There were other "offerings" to pass out in the back, but since Khojaewa was already known and proper introductions had been made it was only fair that the first went to her family. In thanks the large warrior grunted and led them down the way they had come, it was a familiar custom for Inzili and she had seen others do it plenty of times in her youth. After a short walk they reached one of the large dwellings and the warrior pulled the door flap aside, revealing the dimly-lit interior of the central room. There was a fire burning in the rock-lined pit, actually the floor was covered in smooth, flat field stones, and there were a pair of males tending to hocks of meat being roasted.

"You have met my males, Kagg and Didaj, I don't know where the children are."

"Your home is so big," Inzili gasped. There was even a second level at the top, accessible by crude wooden stairs. "How many mates have you claimed?"

"Besides these two and Naena? Two more females, and," she trailed off, glancing at Jhoka before shaking her head. "Kagg. Go get my children."

Sighing the younger looking male stood up and brushed off his knees. "You don't need to act like this because we have company."

Jhoka giggled and looked up at the warrior as she bared her teeth at the male who, unimpressed, just sighed again and wandered off. Stan found that hilarious and loudly chuckled, which earned him an angry shove from his mate.

"I'm sorry, my mate is..." Inzili sighed and shook her head. "You can relate to this. Yes?"

Khojaewa chuckled and looked down at the human with a slow nod. "Yes, but they are handsome so they get away with this insolence."

All three of the females laughed at the remark, but Stan seemed unfazed by it and just gave the warrior a cocky grin. She was easily twice his size, almost a two and a half meters tall and probably triple his body weight; her biceps alone were nearly as big as his head. Both the males were around his height and his build, the older-looking one had more chiseled muscles underneath his thick, scaly hide that was covered in scars. "Kagg" was thinner and a bit shorter, he had more... "feminine" features about him according to Stan's perceptions.

Obviously he was unlike anything she was used to when he met her carnivorous gaze, but he kept it civil and let the grin soften to a smile.

"Meat smells good. Mind tellin' Didaj there," Stan nodded when the male's head shot up at the sound of his name, "that his roast smells mighty fine?"

Good behavior made Inzili grin widely. "My mate asked me to say that the meat smells delicious."

"Hunted it. Seemed good," the male grunted, nodding to Jhoka. "It's for Bewan."

"You make this for father? Thank you so much, Didaj!"

He just grunted and went back to his careful work, so Khojaewa took over for him. "You're a friend... You should be careful, your mother is about-"

A happy squeal interrupted the conversation as the younger male ushered in a small pack of children, one of them clutching some corpse of a small creature that was still bleeding. All total there were seven, two that were clearly the fruit of a union between the older male and Khojaewa but besides that it wasn't clear who was the mother of the others. They were all somewhat different colors, but with the exception of one it was soon obvious that Didaj had fathered the majority of them. Stan figured that's where half those scars came from, they were in the usual places he had to tend to after a vigorous night with his "dragon."
